status: Source qualified locally; maintained patch release and published-consumer adoption are still required.
problem: Root deep signing only signs the current framework version; an updated Chrome with retained older versions produces a private app that fails strict verification. The cache previously trusted only bundle identifier and version.

actualSource.priorPrivateCopiesStrictVerification: fail: embedded framework contains modified or invalid version

correction: Prepare and seal every framework version, nested frameworks first, with one consistent explicit designated requirement per framework.
Strictly verify the complete app before publication and before cached reuse.
Publish a replacement generation without deleting an older cached bundle that may still be running.

A live owned browser retains its validated immutable generation, so additional contexts and browsers avoid repeated full-app verification. Once that owner stops, preparation validates the cache again.
Keep existing browser flags, sandbox and startup/scenario deadlines. Installed Chrome is only read.

regression.fixture: Two real compiled Mach-O framework versions, a source app and a deliberately invalidated cached resource. Real macOS signing and strict verification.
regression.red: One fixture fails at prepared-app strict verification; the pre-existing copy test passes.

preservedFailureEvidence: The original full game battle reached defeat and saved, but its reload assertion timed out.
Fresh standalone launches also exceeded their unchanged deadline while the old copy failed strict verification.
An earlier source test candidate repeated cold signing while disk space fell below 1 GB; that owned run was stopped and its log retained.
The first cache-validation implementation failed the existing warm-session timing check. The live-generation reuse correction passes that same check.
gameStatus: Application issue #193 is implemented and 278 game unit tests pass, but it remains unpushed until the framework release and renewed browser acceptance. Issue #194 separately tracks neutral-granite planning.
scopeLimit: Browser testing infrastructure only. This does not qualify full Gold gameplay, native presentation or every host-load condition.
